record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: For an undirected capacitated network with designated source-sink pairs, is the network coding conjecture true or false; that is, can coding or mixing messages ever beat the throughput permitted by ordinary multicommodity flow?

evidence.quote: In essence, the question is whether or not, for a given undirected graph with capacities on each edge and a set of source-sink pairs, we can send more message bits from each source to its corresponding sink than the network flow should allow if we think of the messages as being generic commodities instead.
Problem 29. Is the network coding conjecture true or false?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph with edge capacities $c:E\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, together with a set of $k$ source–sink pairs $(s_1,t_1),\dots,(s_k,t_k)\in V\times V$. For a rate vector $(r_1,\dots,r_k)\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^k$, say that the rate vector is achievable by multicommodity flow if there exist flows $f_i$ from $s_i$ to $t_i$ of value $r_i$ such that for every edge $e\in E$, $\sum_{i=1}^k |f_i(e)|\le c(e)$ (where each undirected edge of capacity $c(e)$ may carry flow in either direction with total absolute flow at most $c(e)$). Say that the rate vector is achievable by network coding if, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a (block) coding scheme that uses each edge $e$ at average rate at most $c(e)$ (with edges usable in either direction subject to a total capacity constraint) and allows each sink $t_i$ to recover the message of source $s_i$ at rate at least $r_i-\varepsilon$ with vanishing error probability.

The undirected multiple-unicast network coding conjecture asserts that for every such instance, every rate vector achievable by network coding is also achievable by multicommodity flow; equivalently, network coding offers no throughput advantage over multicommodity flow in undirected networks.

Question: Is this conjecture true or false?
artifact.status_search_result: The undirected multiple-unicast network coding conjecture of Li and Li (2004) remains an open problem. Partial progress includes results showing that even an arbitrarily small coding advantage in any undirected instance can be amplified to a near-maximal gap (Braverman–Garg–Schvartzman 2016/17), and that multicommodity flow achieves capacity in certain infinite families of graphs. As of 2025, including recent work on undirected multicast network coding gaps via locally decodable codes, the general conjecture is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Network coding in undirected graphs is either very helpful or not helpful at all
status_evidence.snippet: Even a small advantage over MCF can be amplified to a near-maximum gap; whether any gap exists at all is still unknown.
status_evidence.claim: It is not known whether network coding offers any advantage over multicommodity flow in undirected networks.

status_evidence.title: On the Multiple Unicast Network Coding Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The multiple-unicast network coding conjecture of Li and Li states that network coding equals routing in undirected networks; the conjecture has remained open.
status_evidence.claim: The Li–Li undirected multiple-unicast conjecture is open.

status_evidence.title: Undirected Multicast Network Coding Gaps via Locally Decodable Codes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on coding gaps in undirected networks continues to investigate the conjecture, indicating it remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2025 research treats the undirected coding-vs-flow question as still open.
